title: Two replicas counting in one process
request:
two replicas increment their own entries, then the counter is read

./your_program.sh g-counter
inc r1 5
inc r2 7
value r1
state r1
note: The shape of `state` is entirely yours: the harness never looks inside it, it only hands it to another replica's `merge`. What it must do is round trip, so whatever a replica needs to keep has to be in there.

title: Increments and decrements are counted apart
request:
one replica adds ten and takes three, then another takes twenty

./your_program.sh pn-counter
inc r1 10
dec r1 3
value r1
dec r2 20
value r1
note: Storing 7 as a single number would be the bug. Two G-Counters merge by maximum on each half independently, and the difference is read at the end; one signed number has no maximum that means 'whoever saw more updates'.
